extracted.intended_audience: general Canadian newspaper readers and policymakers (1920s)
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic 1927 Canadian newspaper/magazine page presenting news items, opinion pieces and briefings on public safety, policy, industry, agriculture, science and social issues aimed at a broad lay audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speeding as contributing factor in motor accidents
rubrics_metrics.description: R. L. Fordney's investigation: out of 48,670 motorists involved in accidents last year, 4,979 motor vehicle operators were exceeding the speed limit when the crash took place (approximately eleven per cent). Only two other circumstances — 'shidding' and 'did not have right-of-way' — were reported more frequently than speeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many skidding cases may have arisen out of excess speed. In addition to accidents charged directly to illegal speed, many other accidents would not have occurred had the driver been going too fast for the conditions; infractions such as contesting right-of-way and cutting corners often lead to collisions only because the driver was not keeping the car under control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess speed 'too fast for conditions' as accident contributor
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond illegal speed (exceeding limit), accidents are attributed to drivers going 'too fast for the conditions existing at the time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is used to attribute causation even when the driver was not technically breaking the speed limit — i.e., speed appropriate to posted limit may still be culpable if conditions (weather, road surface, traffic) make it unsafe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government ownership and operation as measure of public success
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion that 'In Canada, government can and does own and run railroads successfully.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as evaluative evidence that public ownership can work in Canada; contrasted with U.S. skepticism. Implied criterion for judging public ownership: practical success of operation and absence of assumed public official ignorance/corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydro-electric policy: users-first principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In Canada they consider the users of hydro-electric power first, even small farmers, and the power companies come last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a positive public-policy criterion (user-priority allocation) versus the criticized alternative where 'power companies come first and the consuming public nowhere.' This is used as a benchmark for evaluating fairness and public interest in power policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabet complexity and literacy (argument for reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief argument used in favor of the change from Arabic to Latin characters in Turkey is that the difficulty of the Arabic is largely responsible for illiteracy in Turkey. The Arabic alphabet has 82 characters, and with positional forms there is an actual total of 96.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy guidance: adopt a simpler alphabet and allow a long transition (15 years) with bilingual printing and new dictionaries. The criterion for change is whether a script's complexity materially impedes literacy and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of clean seed grain as recognized by market uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean, graded, registered seed (Marquis wheat, Victory and Banner oats) handled by the Edmonton Provincial Cleaning and Grading Plant; fully 95 percent of the grain passing through the plant was sold to Alberta farmers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market acceptance (high percentage sold locally) is presented as evidence that 'clean, of good quality and true to variety' seed grain has recognized value. Implicit criterion: seed cleanliness, quality and varietal purity determine commercial value and farmer preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rayon industry: process and raw-material suitability as industrial criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Two processes in Canada: the viscose process (uses bleached sulphite wood pulp) and the cellulose acetate process (uses cotton linters). Canada supplies a large share of world wood pulp; there is hope of applying cellulose acetate treatment to wood pulp to utilize Canadian raw materials entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for industrial planning: availability of domestic raw materials, suitability of manufacturing processes to local inputs, expected energy consumption (hydroelectric), and potential to meet domestic demand before export. Growth potential gauged by import statistics and capacity expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leprosy causation and public-health implication criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Tentative conclusions from Dr. F. L. Walker's investigations: (1) Leprosy is caused by a bacterium related to the fungus actinomyces, and (2) these bacteria enter the body in cuts or wounds about the feet and are not transmitted by the leper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sustained, these scientific findings would require changes of 'great scientific, economic and governmental importance' — i.e., public-health policy and social treatment of lepers should be reassessed based on transmissibility and environmental reservoirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for breeding rust-resistant wheats
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: develop wheat varieties that resist Wheat Stem Rust and still produce satisfactory yields and desired quality. Crosses were made between apparently resistant but otherwise inferior varieties and susceptible high-quality varieties (e.g., Marquis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem characterized as 'complex and complicated' requiring long-term, multidisciplinary research (Rust Research Laboratory established, cooperation with agricultural colleges and U.S. institutions). Evaluation criteria for candidate varieties: rust resistance, yield level, and grain quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banks charging service fees on small accounts — policy argument criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument against levying a service charge on small savings accounts: (1) Canadian banks perform a national public service encouraging thrift among small as well as large wage-earners; (2) while some small accounts operate at a loss initially, many grow into substantial, profitable accounts and valuable connections for the bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy evaluation should weigh public-good objectives (encouraging thrift) and long-term customer value against short-term account profitability. A small fee could discourage thrift and reduce long-term gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immigration medical-inspection policy: minimizing antagonism
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that sending Canadian doctors into Great Britain antagonized British medical men and created a 'blockade' of British immigration; recommendation that roster doctors be used in conjunction with Canadian doctors and that passage fares be reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for immigration medical policy should include diplomatic/host-country acceptance (avoid antagonizing local professionals), procedural cooperation (joint examinations), and consideration of travel cost barriers affecting immigrant selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal definition of 'person' for tax liability
rubrics_metrics.description: As courts interpret the British North America Act, a woman is not a 'qualified person' to sit in the Canadian Senate, but a woman is a 'person' when it comes to paying federal income taxes; the Income War Tax had defined 'Person' to include individuals and groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates that statutory or constitutional terms may be interpreted differently across contexts; criterion for legal classification depends on statutory wording and judicial interpretation — here, tax liability is applied where 'person' is used in a broad sense.
